title: Paper jam
shortDescription: Generic paper jam in paper path.
fullDescription:
Sharp E1 is a general paper jam indicator. The display shows the area on a graphical diagram. Open the indicated door and remove the jammed sheet.

Persistent E1 events may indicate worn pickup rollers or damp paper. Check paper storage conditions.

On MX MFPs, the touch screen guides the user through each jam zone.

fixSteps.title: Clear jam
fixSteps.instruction: Follow on-screen animation to remove paper in direction of travel.

fixSteps.title: Check paper
fixSteps.instruction: Use fresh, dry paper at 80gsm.

faq.q: Can I run the machine right after?
faq.a: Yes, as soon as all fragments are removed.

title: Misfeed in paper tray
shortDescription: Paper not picked from selected tray.
fullDescription:
E2 on Sharp copiers indicates a misfeed at the paper tray — the sheet did not leave the tray at all. Check paper quantity, guide positions, and roller condition.

Reloading paper and fanning the stack solves many E2 events.

Guides set too wide cause skewed pickup and repeated E2 faults.

causes.cause: Paper stack too low or over-limit

fixSteps.title: Reload paper
fixSteps.instruction: Remove stack, fan it, and reload within tray limits.

fixSteps.title: Adjust guides
fixSteps.instruction: Slide guides so they just touch the paper.

whenToCallPro: If guide adjustment does not help.

title: Service call error
fullDescription:
E7 on Sharp MX devices is a generic service-required error. A secondary code (F-code) usually accompanies it, indicating the specific sub-system.

Record the F-code before calling service; it speeds diagnosis.

The machine locks out until cleared by a technician.

fixSteps.title: Record F-code
fixSteps.instruction: Note the full E7-Fxx code shown.

fixSteps.title: Call service
fixSteps.instruction: Contact Sharp authorized service with the F-code.

title: Toner supply error
fullDescription:
F2-02 is a Sharp toner supply error. The motor could not deliver toner to the developer, either due to an empty/caked bottle or failed motor.

Shake and reseat the toner first. If a genuine Sharp cartridge still triggers it, the motor needs service.

fixSteps.title: Reseat toner
fixSteps.instruction: Shake toner bottle 5 times and reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Replace toner
fixSteps.instruction: Install fresh genuine Sharp MX cartridge.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces supply motor.

whenToCallPro: If genuine toner still triggers the code.

title: Toner cartridge not detected
shortDescription: Cartridge IC chip could not be read.
fullDescription:
F2-64 reports that the Sharp MFP cannot read the ID chip on the toner cartridge. It may be missing, poorly seated, or an incompatible aftermarket chip.

Reseat and ensure the cartridge clicks into place.

Install a genuine Sharp MX- toner if aftermarket was in use.

fixSteps.title: Reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinsert cartridge until locked.

fixSteps.title: Use genuine
fixSteps.instruction: Install Sharp OEM cartridge.

faq.q: Do I have to buy Sharp?

title: Fax modem error
fullDescription:
F6-00 indicates a fax modem fault on Sharp MFPs. The modem PCB is not responding or cannot complete fax handshake.

Reseat the fax board and check phone-line connections.

Persistent F6-00 requires fax card replacement.

fixSteps.title: Check phone line
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm dial tone on the connected line.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces fax board.

faq.a: Yes, fax and print are independent.

title: Finisher communication error
shortDescription: Finisher not communicating with main unit.
fullDescription:
F9-02 is Sharp's finisher communication fault. The MFP cannot talk to the attached finisher (stapler/booklet).

Check the finisher connection cable and power; reseat if needed.

A failed finisher PCB requires service.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cable
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, detach and reattach finisher cable.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Technician diagnoses finisher PCB.

whenToCallPro: If cable reseat does not clear.

title: Fusing high temperature
fullDescription:
H4-00 is a fuser overheat safety error on Sharp copiers. The machine locks down to prevent damage.

Same class as L4 — requires technician to diagnose triac or thermistor before clearing.

Do not attempt to restart until serviced.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Leave off until technician arrives.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces faulty components and clears latch via simulation.

faq.a: Yes — a runaway fuser can scorch paper or worse.

title: Main motor lock fail
shortDescription: Main drive motor did not lock to speed.
fullDescription:
L4-01 means the main drive motor did not reach locked speed within timeout. This motor drives drum and paper path.

A jammed drive train or failed motor are causes. Technician inspects gear train and replaces motor if needed.

The MFP is unusable until fixed.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off 1 minute and try again.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Technician replaces motor or clears jam.

title: EEPROM communication error
fullDescription:
U2-40 indicates the Sharp MFP cannot communicate with the EEPROM that stores counters and settings. Corruption or a failed board is typical.

Simulation modes allow re-initialization; otherwise the main PCB is replaced.

Backing up data in advance is recommended for regular maintenance.

fixSteps.title: Simulation reset
fixSteps.instruction: Technician enters simulation 16 to initialize EEPROM.

fixSteps.title: Replace PCB
fixSteps.instruction: If initialization fails, replace main PCB.

faq.a: Yes — technician will rewrite counter values.

title: Developer end of life
fullDescription:
EE-EL signals the developer unit has reached its life limit and must be replaced. Unlike a hard error, Sharp MFPs continue in degraded mode but image quality will drop.

Schedule a developer replacement at service.

Ignoring the warning risks toner contamination and hard faults.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Contact Sharp service for developer replacement.

whenToCallPro: Within a week of the warning.

title: Close door or cover
shortDescription: A cover or door is open.
fullDescription:
CH on Sharp MFPs means a door, cover, or tray is not fully closed. The machine interlock stops operation.

Check front cover, rear cover, manual tray, and duplex unit. A misaligned cover can trigger CH even when it looks closed.

If all covers appear closed, an interlock sensor may be faulty.

fixSteps.title: Check all covers
fixSteps.instruction: Press every door closed until latched.

fixSteps.title: Professional check
fixSteps.instruction: Technician tests interlocks if CH persists.

whenToCallPro: If all covers are closed but CH persists.

faq.a: A safety switch ensuring doors are closed before high voltage engages.
